name: PS-SPLIT
description: PS-SPLIT is a fine-grained benchmark for category discovery by splitting, built from 257 expert-verified taxonomic splits of bird species on iNaturalist, each paired with a taxonomically close control species. It contains 79,061 images of 771 species in 514 coarse classes (257 splitting + 257 control), plus PS-SPLIT-Small (25,285 images, 192 species, 128 coarse classes). It also ships coarse-respecting multi-way splits for CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars and FGVC Aircraft (labels only). Annotations, metadata, splits and SINR location embeddings are released under CC BY-NC 4.0.
citeAs: @inproceedings{lange2026pssplit, title={Predicting Species Splits: A Challenging Fine-Grained Benchmark for Category Discovery}, author={Lange, Christian and Haurum, Joakim Bruslund and Zhao, Bingchen and Mac Aodha, Oisin}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), Evaluations and Datasets Track}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Split events were taken from the iNaturalist taxonomic-changes feed (two-way species splits, each new species with >=20 research-grade observations; split events dated 2013-2024). One control species with no taxonomic change was chosen per split (same genus for 184/257, same family only for 70/257; 3 exceptions documented in the paper appendix). For each species, licensed research-grade observations with a photo were downloaded through the public iNaturalist API in April-May 2026 (first photo of each observation; up to 100 images per splitting species, preferring distinct observers; controls matched to the total of their split). Pipeline code: dataset_construction/ in the code repository.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web API (iNaturalist), citizen-science observations. All images are real photographs; the dataset contains no synthetic or generated data (a VLM is used only to filter images).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images downloaded April-May 2026; observation dates 1963-2026; taxonomic split events 2013-2024.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MegaDetector v5 animal detections with confidence >= 0.75 and shortest box edge >= 190 px are cropped and resized to 256x256. A Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct reviewer answers seven yes/no quality questions (bird present, adult, mostly in frame, in focus, no watermark/text, not an unusual capture, no other prominent animals) and assigns a pose label; only images meeting all criteria are kept. The two species of a split are restricted to their most common shared pose; controls are filtered separately. Visual-difference screen: per candidate split, a logistic-regression probe on frozen, L2-normalised DINOv2 ViT-B/14 (registers) features is trained on a stratified 70% of the split's training-pool images (per-species 80/20 train/test split) and tested on its test-pool images; splits with mean accuracy over 5 seeds below 0.60 were removed (6 of 263). Per-image filter decisions are kept in the metadata CSVs (md_*, vlm_*, dataset_pass).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MegaDetector v5 (crop detection), Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (quality and pose labels), DINOv2 ViT-B/14 with registers (visual-difference screen). Species labels are iNaturalist research-grade community identifications, not machine annotations.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Fine labels are the iNaturalist research-grade species identifications under the post-split taxonomy; coarse labels group the two species of a split (or the single control species). No new human annotation was collected.
rai:dataLimitations: Birds only; PS-SPLIT splits are binary (the FGVC companion splits go up to 30 sub-categories per coarse class). The visual-difference screen keeps only splits a DINOv2 probe can separate above 60% (6/263 removed), so visually indistinguishable splits are under-represented. Probe accuracies near the threshold are noisy (test pools of 5-40 images). Species boundaries follow the iNaturalist taxonomy at download time and may change.
rai:dataBiases: Geographic: observation density follows the distribution of iNaturalist observers rather than of bird species, and some regions have few qualifying splits or controls (paper Appendix F). Selection: the visual-difference screen favours visually separable splits; the VLM filter removes unusual captures and favours typical adult, perched birds (82.3% of splitting-species images, 85.0% of control images are perched), which can reduce intra-species variability. Location features are highly informative for many splits; models may exploit geography rather than appearance. Taxonomic: Passeriformes dominate, as in nature.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Images show birds; crops are centred on the bird, but incidental background content cannot be fully excluded. Metadata include the public iNaturalist user ID of each observer, the observation date, and the latitude/longitude as publicly returned by the iNaturalist API (iNaturalist obscures coordinates for sensitive taxa and on observer request; only these public coordinates are stored). No names or contact details are included. Photographers who want an image removed can open an issue at https://github.com/PS-SPLIT/PSSPLIT/issues.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking category discovery and, specifically, discovery by category splitting: deciding whether a known category should be split, estimating the number of sub-categories, and clustering its images; studying the value of location information for fine-grained discovery. Not intended for, and not validated for, making taxonomic decisions; outputs should at most propose candidate splits for expert review and genetic confirmation.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: supports research on tools that help taxonomists prioritise candidate species splits, relevant to biodiversity monitoring and conservation. Risks are low; misuse could include over-trusting automated split proposals or deriving location information for sensitive species (mitigated because only public, already-obscured coordinates are released).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Hosted on Kaggle with versioning (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/pssplits/ps-splits); the released image set and splits are frozen for reproducibility (later iNaturalist taxonomy changes are not propagated). Code, errata and issue tracker: https://github.com/PS-SPLIT/PSSPLIT. Removal requests from photographers are handled through the issue tracker and released as a new dataset version.

rai:dataCollectionRawData: Original photographs and observation records from iNaturalist (https://www.inaturalist.org), research grade, under the photographers' Creative Commons licences; the URL of each source photo is in the photo_url column of the metadata CSVs.
